title: Kansai in 6 Days — Kyoto, Osaka, Kobe
subtitle: Three nights in Kyoto, three in Osaka: temples, Universal Studios and Dotonbori in six days
summary: An eight-day travelogue squeezed into six: three days based in Kyoto for Kiyomizu-dera, Kinkaku-ji and Arashiyama, then three based in Osaka for Dotonbori, Universal Studios and Kobe. At most four main sights a day, with Osaka Castle, Tsuruhashi, Nintendo OSAKA and Koshien kept as alternates. The notes cover entry, transit cards, Universal Studios reservations and tax-refund reminders.

Actual bus and train times and journey durations.
Travelogue details
Hotels and the order of stops follow the author's trip in May 2023; the original 8 days are squeezed into 6, and Osaka Castle, Tsuruhashi and Nintendo Osaka are left out (see the alternates).
Entry and internet
Before you leave, register your immigration and customs declaration on Visit Japan Web and show the QR code on arrival: https://www.vjw.digital.go.jp/main/#/vjwpco001
Remember your account password or write it down, so you are not locked out at immigration.
For data, use a physical SIM or an eSIM, and switch it on after landing.
Getting around
Trains, subways and buses take Suica or ICOCA transit cards; on an iPhone you can add Suica to Wallet. From the 2023 travelogue: top-up needed a Mastercard, so load it in Taiwan before you leave.

Airport to Kyoto: the JR Haruka limited express, about ¥2,700 one way (official site; fares change from November 2026, so check before you go); the travelogue gives about 1.5 hours, so go by the timetable. Buy your ticket at a ticket machine to be sure of a seat.

Osaka-Umeda to Kansai Airport: the Kansai Airport limousine bus from Hankyu Sanbangai takes about 60 min, ¥1,800 one way, no reservation needed, and runs roughly every 10 to 15 min. With luggage the bus is easier than changing trains.
Around Kyoto you mostly use buses and the Hankyu line; check bus routes and times with your navigation app before you go.
Reservations
Buy Universal Studios Japan tickets early; popular dates can sell out.
Super Nintendo World needs an area timed-entry ticket; see the official site and the park's app for how to get one.
Other
Carry plenty of yen in cash: temple admissions, souvenirs, amulets and some reserved-seat tickets take cash only.
Hanshin Tigers games at Koshien sell out fast; if you want to see one, buy early to match the schedule (see the alternate to-dos).
The tax-refund rules have changed in recent years; check the Japan Tourism Agency's explanation before you leave.
When taking photos, avoid people's faces; shoot temples at an angle; you usually have to carry your rubbish back to the hotel.

notes.title: Trip overview: how the 6 days run
paragraphs: In and out of Kansai Airport, with two nights in Kyoto and three in Osaka, and Kobe and Universal Studios done as day trips from Osaka. Each day holds at most four main stops; Kyoto runs on buses and the Hankyu line, Osaka and Kobe on JR and Hanshin, with one transport card for the lot.
Day 1: land at the airport in the afternoon, ride the Haruka limited express to Kyoto, drop your bags, then go up {@d1-03} in the evening and have ramen at Kyoto Ramen Koji in the station building.
Day 2: a full day in eastern and northern Kyoto, from Yasaka Shrine to {@d2-02}, snacking along Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka, then a bus out to {@d2-04} in the afternoon.
Day 3: Tenryu-ji in Arashiyama and the {@d3-02}, soba for lunch, the monkey park in the afternoon, then back for your bags and the Hankyu line to Osaka Umeda, with yakitori in Sonezaki for dinner.
Day 4: JR to Kobe for {@d4-01} and the waterfront at Meriken Park and Harborland, back to Osaka in the afternoon, then kushikatsu and Don Quijote around {@d4-04} in the evening.
Day 5: all day at {@d5-01}, with the Harry Potter area and the parade, and {@d5-05} in the early evening.
Day 6: the limousine bus from Hankyu Sanbangai to Kansai Airport in the morning, and straight through departures.

Where to sleep: two nights at Toyoko Inn Kyoto Shijo-Omiya, then on day 3 a move to APA Hotel & Resort Osaka Umeda Eki Tower for three nights, with the airport reached straight from Osaka on the last morning.

Getting around: the JR Haruka limited express takes about 80 minutes from the airport to Kyoto; in Kyoto you mostly use buses and the Hankyu line; Osaka to Kobe is the JR Special Rapid, about 22 minutes, and you can return on the Hanshin Main Line through to Osaka Namba; for Universal Studios change to the JR Yumesaki Line from Osaka Station; for the airport, take the limousine bus from Hankyu Sanbangai, about 60 minutes, no reservation needed. Check the latest timetables before you go.

Who it suits: first-timers who want Kyoto's temples, Osaka's food, Kobe's waterfront and Universal Studios in one trip. Book the Universal Studios ticket and the Super Nintendo World area ticket early, and wear comfortable shoes, since the days involve a lot of walking.
